Q: Cannot find module error in Node.js on Windows 11 after npm install A:

This error isn’t actually about React or missing npm modules—it simply means Node.js cannot find the file you’re trying to run. When you execute node app.js from C:\Users\haroo, Node looks for a file named app.js in that exact directory, and since it doesn’t exist there, it throws a MODULE_NOT_FOUND error. The most likely issue is that you’re running the command from the wrong folder. You need to navigate (cd) into the directory where your project and app.js file are located before running the command.

Another possibility is that the file isn’t named app.js at all. Many projects use filenames like index.js or server.js, so it’s worth checking the actual file name using the dir command. Also, if this is a React application, you typically don’t run it with node app.js because React apps are started using scripts like npm start or npm run dev. In short, make sure you’re in the correct directory, verify the file exists with the right name, and use the appropriate command depending on whether it’s a Node backend or a React frontend.

Q: Modify PyQt5 QTextEdit removing newline char (\n) A:

You can use .strip() that will remove leading and trailing character (such as your newline character)

form.textEdit_Title.setText(textEdit_Title.strip() + '  : ' +gmxapi_version)

Q: Java's InheritableThreadLocal equivalent in Python A:

The approach here works for dynamically assigned attributes, but has a limitation when subclassing InheritableLocal.

This implementation relies on copying parent values only when an attribute lookup raises AttributeError. However, threading.local calls __init__ separately in each thread on first access. As a result, attributes initialized in __init__ already exist in the child thread before any lookup occurs.

Because the attribute is already present, no AttributeError is raised, the fallback copy is never triggered, and parent-updated values are not inherited for those attributes.

In practice, this means the approach works when attributes are added dynamically, but not for attributes initialized per-thread via __init__.

Q: The combination of celery chain and group fails A:

Celery is all about batch execution, so your "1." item requirement is already satisfied. Similarly, each Celery task can be sent to ANY queue you want, so "2." requirement is satisfied too.
